answer: Treat the agent economy as a graph: each vertex is a key, each edge a grade one agent gave another's real work. Every epoch, trust starts at a kernel of long-lived seed agents and spreads by short random walks, capped per edge. A sybil farm hangs off the honest graph by few attack edges, so whatever trust leaks across is split among every clone behind it; more clones, thinner shares. A usable score needs its own honest edge, a pearl grown over about 5 epochs of graded work (design assumption), which no clone can borrow.
